subject: Re: Pricing follow-up & regional residency (FintechCo)
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: pricing & regional residency (FintechCo)

Hi Sarah —

Great to meet earlier today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and I can follow up with a clear pricing/ops plan: 

- Estimated monthly token volume: ~500M tokens/month (mix: ~70% generation, 30% embeddings/semantic search).
- Your stated budget range: $20k–$30k/month initially; goal to get unit economics closer to $X per 1M tokens.
- Residency requirement: primary data residency in EU (customer data and logs must remain in EU).
- Key asks: SOC2 evidence, procurement timeline (PO vs contract), and whether you need SSO/IdP + audit logs.

Attached: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf (initial rate cards) and SOC2_summary.pdf. I’ve pulled a high-level regional delta below so you have the numbers to evaluate:

Regional unit economics (ballpark, illustrative):
- US region baseline: $0.80 per 1M tokens (on our hosted API list rates for gen-heavy workloads).
- EU region uplift: ~20% => ~ $0.96 per 1M tokens (driven by multi-region infra + compliance controls).
- Reserved/dedicated commitment (12mo) discounts: ~18–25% off listed rates (so US committed ~ $0.62–0.66 /1M, EU committed ~ $0.78–0.83 /1M).

Notes on how to get to your target economics:
- Prefix/KV caching and workload-aware batching we discussed can reduce effective consumption by ~10–25% depending on prompt reuse.
- Shifting more inference to embeddings for retrieval-heavy UX reduces per-engagement token spend.
- Reserved capacity + committed usage and a 12-month billing cadence gives the steepest unit discounts.

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm the monthly token estimate (500M) and desired contract cadence (monthly trial vs 12m commit).
2) I’ll run a modeled pricing worksheet tuned to your token mix and expected cache hit rates and share a committed vs on-demand comparison.
3) Marissa will loop in procurement resources and send SOC2 + legal starter pack if you want to move toward PO.

Are you available early next week for a quick procurement + SRE alignment call? Happy to include our EU infra lead to walk through data residency controls.

Thanks again —

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf (pricing sheet), SOC2_summary.pdf (summary)

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Jun 2027 17:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing & regional residency (FintechCo)

Thanks, Dylan — this is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token estimate is a working number: 500M/month is our current projection for Q4 run-rate (could be +/- 20%).
- Budget: our finance partner signed off on a $20k–$30k/mo operational budget right now. To commit to 12mo we’d need to justify savings vs the shorter-term spend.
- Residency: we need EU residency for processing and logs; vendor must demonstrate EU-only storage for customer data and provide export controls.

Can you confirm the committed (12mo) rate per 1M tokens for EU if we lock to 500M/month? Also please share SOC2 artifacts and an intro to your EU infra lead.

Procurement notes: procurement@fintechco.com will manage the PO path; typical timeline is 3–4 weeks once we have pricing and a draft SOW. We also require vendor SSO and SCIM support.

Best,
Sarah Li
Head of ML Integrations | FintechCo
sarah.li@fintechco.com

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Jun 2027 09:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing & regional residency (FintechCo)

Sarah — thanks. See concrete numbers below based on the 500M/mo baseline and EU residency requirement. I’m including a modeled worksheet (attached) but pulled the headline below so you can review quickly.

Modeled unit economics (500M tokens/mo):
- On-demand hosted (US): list $0.80 / 1M tokens => monthly cost ~ $400.00 * 500 = $200,000 (note: this is illustrative; your mix reduces effective spend).
- On-demand hosted (EU): list $0.96 / 1M tokens (~20% uplift) => monthly cost ~ $480 * 500 = $240,000.

Committed (12mo) pricing (illustrative committed discounts applied):
- Committed US rate: $0.65 / 1M => monthly ~ $325 * 500 = $162,500.
- Committed EU rate: $0.78 / 1M => monthly ~ $390 * 500 = $195,000.

Important clarifications:
- The big lever here is effective tokens consumed (after cache/batching). With good caching strategies your effective billable tokens can be 15–25% lower than raw generation tokens, bringing committed EU cost closer to your $/1M target.
- We also offer reserved capacity (Dedicated) where throughput guarantees plus a longer commit can further drop unit price — we can model Dedicated options if you want predictable latency and lower $/1M.

Given your $20k–$30k/month operational budget, two paths to explore:
A) Start on on-demand EU (trial) to validate usage and optimize prompts/caching; then convert to committed to capture discounts once you hit predictable run-rate.
B) If you can accelerate to a 12mo commit with a PO, we can structure a tailored committed rate that approaches your target unit economics — I’ll have our pricing ops run scenarios with Marissa.

Next steps I’ll take today: 
- Share modeled worksheet with committed vs on-demand comparisons (attached: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf updated).
- Pull SOC2 artifacts and make intros to our EU infra lead + security contact.
- Set a procurement + SRE alignment call — can propose times early next week.

Can you and procurement do Tue 15 Jun 2027 10:00–11:00 CET or Wed 16 Jun 09:00–10:00 CET?

Thanks — I’ll include draft SOW language in the next email.

Dylan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_pricing_sheet_v3.pdf, EU-data-residency-notes.docx

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@fintechco.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 10:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: pricing & regional residency (FintechCo)

Thanks — Tue 15 Jun 2027 10:00 CET works for procurement and our infra lead. Please include the EU infra contact and a one-page SOW / proposed PO terms ahead of the call so procurement can review.

Also can you confirm whether Redwood supports SP-initiated SSO + SCIM provisioning? That’s a must-have for us.

We’ll look at the modeled worksheet and come prepared with expected cache hit assumptions. If the committed EU numbers get within ~15% of the US committed cost, I can push the 12mo approval internally.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Sarah Li
